title: Feature-slice sprint notes: rapid gated experiments
content:
Quickbrain: goal is a tiny, repeatable flow for carving out a narrow feature slice, shipping it to a tiny percentage of traffic, and learning fast (K=3 experiments per sprint).

Why: long features take forever; teams need a way to validate interaction assumptions and perf/cost impact before full rollout. This is a personal scratchpad + lightweight proto for 2-week sprint experiments.

Core idea (one-liner): define a minimal surface (API + UX endpoint + metrics) that can be toggled and observed independently, with automatic rollback if latency/cost/quality triggers fire.

Principles / constraints:
- Keep model/runtime changes minimal: prefer routing + micro-policy over model edits.
- Must be reversible in < 10m (feature off / traffic drained).
- Instrumentation first: every slice includes golden prompt set and automatic micro-eval.
- Cost SLO guardrails by default (per-request estimated token cost).
- Default to 0.5–2% traffic for initial slices.

Proposed pieces (minimal MVP):
1) Slice definition format (YAMLish):
   - id: stable id
   - route: API route or front-end flag
   - matchers: simple traffic selectors (user cohorts / tenant / header / cookie)
   - model_variant: optional override
   - budget: per-minute token cap or $ cap
   - metrics: list of metric ids to stream
   - rollback_triggers: latency > X ms, error rate > Y, quality drop > Z

2) Quick toggle UI (Console microview):
   - small card: name, traffic % slider, start/stop, last 24h metrics sparkline
   - quick notes field, owner, expected duration

3) Runtime routing hooks:
   - evaluate matchers at proxy edge, short-circuit to slice if matched
   - ensure KV cache compatibility across slices (avoid sticky state mismatch)

4) Safety net / auto-rollbacks:
   - streaming alerting rule that marks slice as degraded and flips to fallback variant
   - background drain job: stop assigning new requests to slice and wait 30s for in-flight to finish

5) Micro-eval harness:
   - run a small prompt set on every candidate model variant; store pass/fail and average score
   - tie to alert trigger: if eval score drops > 5% relative to baseline, mark for rollback

Success metrics (for the experiment itself):
- Time from slice creation -> first telemetry visible < 10m
- Canary failure rate <= baseline + 1.5x in first 24h
- Observed decision: ship (expand), iterate (tweak), or kill within 7 days

Example user stories (short):
- As a product PM, I can create a feature slice that targets 1% of traffic and attach an eval set so I can validate output quality without risking all users.
- As an SRE, I can set an automatic per-slice token budget so an experiment can never exceed $X/day.
- As an engineer, I can add a route matcher that targets only enterprise tenants in eu-west and see a small dashboard for requests routed.

Implementation sketch (phased):
Phase 0: manual wires + router flag prototype (1 sprint)
- engineer sets header+flag at proxy; small dashboard reading logs via query
Phase 1: slice config + console toggle + light automation (2 sprints)
- schema, console card, simple routing policy, per-slice metrics in Console
Phase 2: auto-rollbacks + micro-eval integration + cost budgeting (2 sprints)
Phase 3: templated slices + experiment library + infra for stateful slices (4 sprints)

Open questions / parking lot:
- How to handle slices that must modify model prompts (prompt plumbing + provenance)?
- Sticky sessions and cached KV: do we enforce sticky hash or forbid stateful slices?
- Metrics signal design: how do we avoid false positives in quality evals for small sample sizes?
- Ownership model: should slices be namespaced per-team with quota?
- Billing/chargeback: how to show per-slice cost to owning team?

Immediate next actions (for next 48h):
- Draft minimal slice schema (YAML) and post to #product-experiments for feedback (me)
- Spike a console toy: card + slider (Drew)
- Wire up a Prometheus query for per-slice QPS / p95 / estimated tokens (Maya)

Notes to self:
- Keep scope small; shipping a toggle + visible metrics is > 80% of value.
- Reuse existing rollout code where possible (canary infra?).
- Think through user privacy for per-tenant evals.

References / potential hubs:
- look at: GH PR#412 (feature-slice proto)
- convo: #product-experiments, #sre-rollouts
- similar idea: "mini canaries" notes in infra/sre drive (find later)

End-of-scratchpad.

(rough, fragmented — will polish into a 1-pager once spikes land)
